newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end sharply lower on FOMC minutes.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end sharply lower on FOMC minutes.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished sharply lower, with the long-end violating critical support levels on renewed concerns the Federal Reserve may tighten rates in September, traders and analysts said.
Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) July 2-3 meeting rattled an already nervous U.S. bond and Eurodollar futures markets at the opening of the week.
The minutes showed the committee voted 11 to one to keep short-term U.S. interest rates steady with a bias towards tightening.
"It dawned on people that the market wasn't priced for a possible Federal Reserve action," said Peter McTeague, a market strategist at MCM Tradewatch.
"There was almost an assumption that the Fed was going to stay on hold," one trader said. "But with the asymmetrical proposal that certainly leads to more uncertainty as to the September meeting."
September T-bonds closed below the 100-day moving average at 108-24/32 after the contract violated that level late in the day on light selling pressure.
However, analysts and traders said light volume could not be blamed for the sharp extended slide in the T-bond contract.

"We spent a long time building a base from the 105-16/32 level to 112-16/32," one bond futures floor source said. "We haven't been able to re-test the 112-00 level, which makes it look like that pop was a short squeeze."

McTeague noted that September bonds have not closed below its 100-day moving average during August and the contract is poised to hit the July 30 low of 107-22/32 this week. The 107-22/32 is roughly equivalent to 7.10 percent in the cash bond yield.

Trade was more active in the morning after U.S. bond futures opened after a delay. One firm sold 3,000 September bonds at the 109-04/32 level, which touched off panic selling in bonds and then Eurodollars, traders said.
Locals were also reportedly pushing the market lower, as bonds touched off sell-stop orders every two to three ticks, floor sources said.

Concerns about the possibility of a Federal Reserve tightening ahead of the Presidential elections this fall also heightened the market's attention on next Friday's U.S. August nonfarm payrolls report and unemployment rate.
"The market is discounting that a third-quarter slowdown may not be there," one trader said, noting that spreading three-month to two-year note market was active earlier in the day.

As a result, he expects the short-end of the market to stabilize, while bonds further extend losses and steepen the yield curve. He said swaps-related trade could account for the fact that swap spreads narrowed.
At the end of pit trade, September bonds were down 29/32 at 108-20/32, December Eurodollars were down eight bps at 94.07 and March Eurodollars were off 11 bps at 93.90.
